subject: Private offer: regional price cushion, local tax handling, and reseller brokerage flow
messages:
From: CloudBridge Procurement <procurement@cloudbridge.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@cloudbridge.com>
Date: 2028-09-04T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Private offer draft and a couple clarifying tax questions

Sofia —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached is the private offer worksheet the procurement team asked to see for internal approval. Two quick clarifying items before we run this up the chain:

1) Local tax treatment: our counsel flagged that list-price cushions (we call them a "buffer") could create VAT/taxable event concerns in some EMEA subsidiaries if not documented as a non-consideration adjustment. Can you confirm how Redwood labels these cushions on the invoice and whether you can provide a one-line statement for our tax team?

2) Reseller brokerage: we plan to route this through a reseller in our APAC region. We need to understand whether reseller brokerage (a 6% pass-through fee) should be deducted from the private offer net revenue or handled as a downstream credit. Our finance wants the cleanest path for recognition.

Attached: CloudBridge_PrivateOffer_v1.pdf (worksheet)

Appreciate a quick reply — procurement is aiming for approval on Friday.

— Elena
Elena Martins
Finance Director, CloudBridge
[Attachment: CloudBridge_PrivateOffer_v1.pdf (PDF)]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martins <elena.martins@cloudbridge.com>, CloudBridge Procurement <procurement@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-04T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer draft and a couple clarifying tax questions

Elena — thanks for the note and the worksheet. A few quick points, and looping Ben for the reseller flow: 

1) Invoice labeling and tax: Redwood invoices private-offer adjustments as a non-product billing adjustment and we include an explicit line that reads: "Contractual pricing adjustment — no change to delivered services or additional consideration." We can provide a short template statement for your tax team and are willing to include the same line on the invoice copy prior to submission.

2) Buffer / list-price cushion mechanics: the cushion lives in our private-offer waterfall as a holdback that reduces the list price for settlement purposes but does not change the underlying SKU pricing that was delivered. In jurisdictions where tax treatment is sensitive, we can instead flow the same uplift as a credit memo mechanism — happy to coordinate with your tax contact if you prefer that path.

3) Reseller brokerage: @Ben — can you advise on how Redwood typically shows reseller brokerage on our back-office and whether the brokerage is visible on our revenue exports (Hub DB) versus being a downstream settlement between partner and customer?

I'll draft the one-liner and send it over in the next email.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Director, Strategic GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Elena Martins <elena.martins@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-04T10:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer draft and a couple clarifying tax questions

Elena, Sofia — quick answers from ops/finance perspective: 

- Reseller brokerage (6%): Redwood does not reduce recognized revenue on the Redwood invoice for partner brokerage unless Redwood is the party paying the reseller. In the standard reseller pass-through model, Redwood invoices CloudBridge for the net private-offer price and the reseller arranges downstream settlement with CloudBridge. That means CloudBridge's accounting should treat the brokerage as a separate procurement cost (vendor/commission), not as a Redwood revenue reduction.

- For downstream visibility, we can provide an "invoice routing statement" showing the gross list price, private-offer adjustment, and net invoiced amount (no brokerage deduction). That export is what Hub DB surfaces for your audit team.

- If CloudBridge requires the brokerage to be reflected as a netback on our invoice for internal policy reasons, we can accommodate via a customer-level credit memo flow, but that will create different recognition timing (we should discuss with both sides' revenue teams).

I'll attach the invoice-line template and a sample CSV export. 

Regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Deal Ops, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: reseller_invoice_template.txt; reseller_fee_matrix.xlsx]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Martins <elena.martins@cloudbridge.com>, CloudBridge Procurement <procurement@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-09-04T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer draft and a couple clarifying tax questions

Elena — attached is a short template statement you can share with tax: 

"Redwood Inference confirms that the private-offer pricing adjustment is a contractual, non-consideration pricing adjustment and does not constitute additional goods or services. The adjustment will be documented on the invoice as a contractual pricing adjustment and will not change the nature or timing of service delivery."

Ben also attached the invoice routing export and reseller matrix for your review. If that language works for tax, we can proceed with the private offer as-is and you can route procurement approval. If not, tell us whether you prefer an invoice credit memo flow and we'll scope the accounting delta.

Next steps I recommend:
- Elena: confirm tax OK with the one-liner (or request credit memo path)
- Elena/Procurement: confirm whether you want brokerage reflected on Redwood invoice or handled as downstream settlement
- Ben/Laura: prepare final private-offer PDF with chosen treatment and send for signature

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Sofia
[Attachment: pricing_adjustment_statement.txt]

From: CloudBridge Procurement <procurement@cloudbridge.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@cloudbridge.com>, Elena Martins <elena.martins@cloudbridge.com>
Date: 2028-09-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer draft and a couple clarifying tax questions

Sofia/Ben — thanks, that helps. Tax reviewed the wording and requested a minor edit to explicitly say "no taxable consideration" and asked for a signed PDF with the statement visible on the invoice sample.

Separately, procurement prefers the reseller brokerage to be handled downstream (i.e., not reflected as a deduction on Redwood's invoice) so their vendor payments team can track the commission separately. They asked whether Redwood can provide a short evidence file (a CSV row) showing gross list price, private-offer adjustment, and net invoice per PO line for their audit.

Goal: procurement needs the signed private offer PDF + the CSV evidence by EOD Wednesday to meet our internal cutover.

— Amit
[Attachment: none]
